decisionMemo.businessProblem: A profitable $20M boutique consulting firm has hit a growth plateau (18% -> 6% YoY) with flat billing rates, sub-target utilization (~68%), and partners at full delivery capacity. To durably raise growth and margin it must choose a direction within ~90 days among (A) consolidating via acquisitions of smaller competitors to build scale (requiring outside growth capital and dilution), (B) specializing deeper into a defensible niche to win pricing power and thought leadership (slower top-line but higher rates), or (C) pivoting to add implementation/managed services for higher-margin, more recurring revenue (new delivery model and unproven economics). The choice is partly irreversible (a capital raise and roll-up, a brand repositioning, or a delivery-model build all reshape the firm and its partner-compensation model), and it is not yet established whether the plateau is fundamentally a pricing/positioning problem, a demand problem, or a delivery-capacity/model problem - which is precisely what should determine the right strategy.
